exact_statement: for all n, k with 0 <= k <= n, C(n, k) >= n
success_condition: no counterexample in the stated range
failure_condition: any (n, k) in range with C(n, k) < n

bounded_search.predicate: k > n or comb(n, k) >= n

_why: Known FALSE: k = 0 gives C(n,0) = 1 < n for every n > 1. A single-variable sweep cannot express this claim at all, so it also checks that the product search is really enumerating the second axis rather than defaulting it.
